title: Core definitions
description: Shared $defs for every schema in this repository. Referenced as core.defs.schema.json#/$defs/<name>. Scores and rubrics are deliberately absent: consumers that want them extend their own schemas.

schema_version.title: Schema version
schema_version.description: Every document declares its schema version; concrete schemas narrow this to a const.

identifier.title: Identifier
identifier.description: Stable machine identity. Whitespace-only and empty identifiers are rejected by construction.

digest.title: Content digest
digest.description: Lowercase hex SHA-256 with an explicit algorithm prefix.

timestamp.title: UTC timestamp
timestamp.description: RFC 3339 in UTC; local offsets are rejected so run records sort globally.

criterion_result.title: Criterion result
criterion_result.description: NOT_RUN and INCONCLUSIVE exist so that unchecked criteria can never be reported as passing.

evidence_kind.title: Evidence kind
evidence_kind.description: probe marks an executed adversarial check; a negative-path claim requires one.

evidence_ref.title: Evidence reference
evidence_ref.description: One logged piece of evidence. Claims point at these by id.

ref.description: The command line, path, pointer, or citation the evidence came from.

finding.title: Finding
finding.description: A defect claim with evidence and the smallest action that resolves it.

negative_path_claim.description: True when the claim asserts that something invalid is rejected. Such claims require an executed probe among the evidence refs.

criterion_outcome.title: Criterion outcome
criterion_outcome.description: One acceptance criterion mapped to evidence.

non_claims.title: Non-claims
non_claims.description: What this document explicitly does not assert. At least one is mandatory: a PASS is bounded by its non-claims.

side_effect.title: Side effect
side_effect.description: What the step touched. 'Nothing' is declared explicitly as kind none, never by omission.

candidate.title: Candidate identity
candidate.description: What was produced or reviewed, pinned by digest. Provenance (git commit, artifact store) is carried by the referencing schema, not baked in here.
